newsitem.title: UK: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell plans hiring drive.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell plans hiring drive.

text.p: Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) is poised to start the second leg of an ambitious hiring programme intended to propel it to a leading position in British and European equities, DMG executives say.

The investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank has already hired some 60 equities staff in London, in the process sparking claims of fueling a wage inflation spiral in the London securities industry.

But DMG, which denies paying inflated salaries to lure top analysts and traders, has so far hired mainly pan-European analysts and the hiring of more specific UK specialists has yet to begin in earnest.

DMG's head of UK equities John Smith, who joined Morgan Grenfell earlier this month after quitting as head of European research at UBS, said in an interview the firm planned to hire more equities staff in London.

"We plan to take on probably another 40 in the UK business," Smith said. "We have particularly got a lot to do on the research side." Back office settlement and trade confimation staff are also be among those being sought.
The recruitment drive is the latest stage of DMG's move to grab a slice of equity trading in London, first set out last year by Deutsche -- Europe's biggest bank in terms of assets.

The firm plans to start equity market-making in the first quarter of 1997. Already mostly in place is a European sales trading team under Nick Feingold, who joined from Natwest, an equity trading team under Phil Hylander from SBC Warburg, and an equity sales team under Mark Rutherford -- like Smith from UBS.
Smith said he believes DMG and its parent have a strong enough position to enable them to secure a share of the increasingly competitive London equity market.
He said DMG had already won recognition for its research output in continental Europe, as well as securing a strong position in corporate advisory work on European mergers and acquisitions.
"I don't think anyone has ever tried to build an equities business with the advantages we have, the franchise of Morgan Grenfell and the resources of Deutsche Bank," Smith said.
"That's why we have able to attract so many high calibre people."
Smith admitted the going would be tough, however, as he aims to compete against established giants such as Merrill Lynch, SBC Warburg and NatWest Markets.
He said DMG's aim was to offer a cost-effective pan-European research and equity trading service which was closely tailored to the requirements of institutional investors.
"I don't think people have been delivering the service customers want, people are not happy with the quality of research and I know people not happy with liquidity in the London market," he said.
Smith said DMG's start-up status in equities was also an important advantage, saying the "discipline of hiring" was another was of ensuring a top-quality team.
"We only have to hire people who are outstanding and that is an incredible advantage to have," he said.
Smith denied Morgan Grenfell had lured staff with bumper salary offers. "Investment banking is expensive if (you) want to be one of the leaders, you can't do it on a shoestring," he said.
"But there will continue to be rigorous control and this is easier than buying an existing player."
"It is a cheap option provided it is successful," he said, "I'm confident about the economics, I think it will be a very good business but only providing we do what the customer wants."
